Yes—you should be able to spot the Moon.

It is very high in the sky, at about **58° altitude** and **azimuth 193°**—roughly toward the **south-southwest**, well above the horizon. At **42% illumination**, it presents a substantial bright crescent/half-moon, and its angular separation from the Sun is about **81°**, far enough that sunlight should not make it exceptionally difficult to see.

The bright daylight sky will reduce contrast, but a Moon this high and illuminated is normally visible to unaided eyes, especially under clear conditions. Look toward the south-southwest, about two-thirds of the way from the horizon to overhead; blocking direct sunlight and scanning slowly should help. Avoid looking anywhere near the Sun itself.
